source.title: Effect of pre-training scale on intra- and inter-domain, full and few-shot transfer learning for natural and X-Ray chest images

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present; the text is not cut off or garbled.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether scaling pretraining changes downstream transfer performance, using supervised ResNet pretraining and image-classification or X-ray transfer metrics rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream accuracy and AUC across pretraining model sizes, data scales, domains, and transfer-shot settings. It does not measure language-model loss or fit power laws. Its power-law and compute-optimal claims in the background are cited context, not results of this study. Few-shot figures are described qualitatively in the text; recorded those reported aggregate statements separately rather than estimating values from plots.
record.test_reason: Supervised ResNet image pretraining (2 sizes × 2 data scales per domain) with transfer accuracy/AUC reported. This bears on V6's 'downstream improves with scale' in a new setting (vision, natural and X-ray targets). No law is fitted and no pretraining loss is related to downstream scores, so 'predictably' is untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Correction: few-shot gains are absent for medical-medical as well as inter-domain transfer; intra-domain medical gains are concentrated in full shot. Addition: R152x4 pretrained on ImageNet-21k matches or beats medical-pretrained models on large X-ray targets.
record.recipe_differences: Uses supervised ResNet image classification pretraining, then fine-tunes on natural-image or X-ray targets and measures accuracy or mean AUC. It does not use language models, held-out cross-entropy scaling-law fits, compute-optimal allocation, or loss extrapolation.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer outcomes vary by source-target domain alignment, target dataset size, full-shot versus few-shot regime, pretraining model size, and pretraining dataset scale. The authors also note that the BiT-HyperRule may bias fine-tuning settings toward natural-image targets.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network (long version); the text also notes a short version published in MedNeurIPS 2021.
record.problems: Only two ResNet sizes are tested, and the study uses supervised classification and available public datasets; it does not fit scaling laws or establish predictability. Few-shot results have larger variance and are largely shown in figures. The authors state that BiT-HyperRule may bias fine-tuning toward natural-image targets, and acknowledge limits on larger models, larger datasets, architectures, and unsupervised pretraining.
record.rows_left_out: No Table 2 result rows were omitted. Individual few-shot figure values were not transcribed because the prose does not specify them numerically; the reported qualitative aggregate outcomes are captured in r49-r51.

untested.parts: Predictability: no fitted curve, no prediction of larger runs, and no relation of downstream score to pretraining loss. Only two model sizes and two data scales per domain.
No language models and no held-out pretraining loss scaling.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
Vision pretraining is used, but no power-law form is fitted.

missing.what: Per-target full-shot values for the large X-ray targets (MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert, PadChest, PadChest-Cl, NIH) across S-MED/L-MED/1K/21K × R50x1/R152x4. Includes the PadChest R152x4 medical data-scale non-improvement (75.91→75.23), which is currently only aggregated in r52.
Intermediate medical superset steps (CheXpert → +MIMIC → +NIH → +PadChest), showing flattening or no gain when NIH is added.

record.verdict_notes: Vision-only study with two model sizes and two data scales per domain. It shows monotone-ish improvement, not a predictable law. The record's supports condition mislabels the S-MED/L-MED→natural-target rows as medical-medical; they are the grayed medical-natural control. Several 'reversed' and 'observed' states on small targets are within reported noise.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss or power-law relationship is measured.
No small-run fit or prediction of larger-run loss is performed.
No fixed-compute budget or compute-optimal allocation between model parameters and training tokens is studied.
The study compares two ResNet sizes but does not isolate depth, width, or other architecture effects at fixed parameter count.
Image models and supervised transfer are studied, but the study does not test whether the same power-law form holds in those settings.
The study reports downstream transfer metrics for selected vision models and targets, but does not test a predictive law relating those metrics to pretraining loss or fit a general scaling curve.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal split are fitted or compared across fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Full-shot natural-natural transfer (both model and data scale), plus natural-natural few-shot
relationships.reason: ImageNet-21k and R152x4 raise accuracy on all natural targets except Pets at R152x4 (r4, r7, r8, r12, r15, r16, r20, r23, r24, r28, r31). Few-shot gains reach 20–30 points (r49).
relationships.display_finding: ImageNet-21k pretraining and R152x4 improved natural-target accuracy except for Pets at R152x4, with few-shot gains reaching 20–30 points.

relationships.condition: Full-shot medical-medical transfer, and natural-medical transfer to large X-ray targets
relationships.reason: Scale gains on COVIDx and Tuberculosis from medical sources (r34, r37, r38, r42, r46). Consistent gains on large X-ray targets (r52; Table 2 values not rowed).
relationships.display_finding: Scaling improved COVIDx and Tuberculosis performance with medical pretraining and consistently improved transfer to large X-ray targets.

relationships.condition: Medical-natural control transfer (medical source to natural targets), full shot
relationships.reason: Larger model raises scores in the control setting (r5, r13, r21, r29), and data scale mostly helps (r2, r6, r10, r14, r30).
relationships.display_finding: Larger models improved transfer scores, and larger pretraining datasets usually helped.

relationships.condition: Few-shot medical-medical and natural-medical transfer; full-shot natural-medical transfer to small X-ray targets
relationships.reason: Authors report no clear or systematic scale gain (r50, r51). Small-target model and data changes are within noise (r39, r40, r47, r48).
relationships.display_finding: Scaling produces no clear or systematic improvement, with model and data changes on small targets remaining within noise.

relationships.condition: Isolated data-scale or model-scale increases at fixed setting
relationships.reason: No gain or slight drops: Pets R152x4 (r32), Flowers from medical sources (r18, r22), Tuberculosis S-MED with the larger model (r45). Also PadChest medical-medical with R152x4 (Table 2, not rowed).
relationships.display_finding: Isolated increases in data or model size yield no improvement or slight declines on Pets, Flowers, Tuberculosis, and PadChest in the tested settings.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: Larger models or larger source datasets raise transfer scores in most reported comparisons; see r2-r8, r10-r16, r20-r21, r23-r24, r26-r31, r34-r40, r42, r44, r46-r47 and aggregate r52.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Few-shot medical-medical and natural-medical transfer; full-shot transfer to some small targets and selected model/data settings
